newsitem.title: CROATIA: IMF says Croatia aid talks hinge on 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Croatia aid talks hinge on 1997 budget.

text.p: Talks between Croatia and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on a three-year programme of financial support could be completed soon but they hinge on delayed budget plans, an IMF chief of mission said on Monday.

"There have been some delays in the past but we are returning in December to finalise negotiations on the extended fund facility (EFF)," Robert Feldman told a news conference at the end of a two-week visit to Croatia.
An IMF 18-month stand-by arrangement to back the Croatian stabilisation programme expired this spring. The fund had been expected to approve new EFF some time this autumn.

While praising the country's economic performance for the current year, Feldman said exact projections for further aid through to 1997 would have to be based on the government's sound economic and fiscal policies for the next three years.
"The budget for 1997 has not been fully articulated or submitted," he said, adding he hoped local authorities would complete and present it by December.
Feldman said Croatia needed such a budget which would cover its reconstruction social welfare needs while not overshooting sustainable growth.
A budget deficit of up to 2.5-3.0 percent at most would be reasonable so as not to pile up the country's external debt, he said.

On the basis of indicators reviewed during the mission, the IMF predicted real growth at a rate of at least five percent in 1996. Cautiously upgrading previous forecasts, Feldman hinted that even a seven percent figure might be possible.
He was full of praise for Croatia's moderate inflation of 3.5 percent to August, stable rate of the domestic currency, the kuna, and solid central bank foreign exchange reserves.
The international reserves have increased to reach the country's 2.5-month total imports, he said.

"The monetary policy for next year would also have to assume the exchange rate stability and in addition...keep a firm eye on price stability to avoid pressure on prices," Feldman said. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
